law: A production script under scripts/ is either wired through a declared channel (the gate manifest, an npm lifecycle chain, or a job in ci.yml) or it is registered HERE as a hand-run tool, with a reason and an owner. There is no third state. Before WO-CAN-02 there was one: the wiring gate counted every package.json alias as a channel, so twenty-plus checks nobody had ever run counted as covered, and this gate's own docblock claimed exclusions (tests, lib/, codemods/, quality-evidence/) that its walk never applied.
rules: An entry must name a file that exists; a dead entry fails the gate.
An entry must carry a reason and an owner; a bare path is not an exception.
An entry must NOT also be named by a channel: registering something CI already runs would hide the real wiring.
Registration is not permission to rot. Every owner below is a work order that either wires the tool or deletes it.

workspaceLaw: A hand-run tool that lives OUTSIDE this package's scripts/ census is declared here as a workspaceTool. The declaration grants no exemption in any census -- there is nothing to excuse, because the file was never counted -- so it cannot become a laundering channel. What it does is make the claim CHECKABLE: the file must exist, it must carry a reason and an owner, and it must be named by NO channel (the gate manifest, any package.json script in the workspace, or ci.yml). Wire one of these into CI and this gate fails until the declaration is removed; delete one and it fails on the ghost.
